children.why_this_cut: Front matter, overview, red-line principles, general principles, risk taxonomy, levels of authority, and definitions. The only crossing linkage is the authority-levels concept (root/system/developer/user/guideline ordering), which is established at L69-101 and used throughout the rest of the document; seeded below.

Chain of command section (L171-795) plus the start of Stay in bounds through the restricted content subsections (L797-1120). The chain of command establishes the authority ordering and the candidate-instruction filtering machinery that the stay-in-bounds rules rely on; the cut at L1120 lands at a blank line after the restricted content section, before the sensitive content section begins.

Remainder: sensitive content, risky situations, privileged information, fairness, real-world ties, seek the truth, best work, style, voice mode, and under-18 principles. This is a large span but the internal structure is a sequence of independent principle sections; the only cross-boundary dependencies are the authority-level ordering and the stay-in-bounds content categories, both seeded below.

seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: which of two authority levels outranks the other (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority)

seed_vocabulary.name: chain_of_command
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle that higher-authority instructions override lower-authority ones, and the mechanism for identifying and following applicable instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: candidate_instructions
seed_vocabulary.prose: all instructions in the Model Spec plus unquoted plain text in system, developer, and user messages, each assigned the authority level of its containing section or message

seed_vocabulary.name: applicable_instructions
seed_vocabulary.prose: candidate instructions that are not misaligned with a higher-level instruction, superseded by a later same-level instruction, or suspected to be mistaken

seed_vocabulary.name: stay_in_bounds_content_categories
seed_vocabulary.prose: the three categories of disallowed content: prohibited content (sexual content involving minors), restricted content (information hazards and sensitive personal data), and sensitive content (erotica and gore) in specific circumstances

seed_vocabulary.name: transformation_exception
seed_vocabulary.prose: the exception allowing the assistant to transform or analyze content the user directly provided, even if the output would ordinarily be disallowed as restricted or sensitive content

seed_vocabulary.name: scope_of_autonomy
seed_vocabulary.prose: the clear, mutually understood scope of autonomy shared between the assistant and the user, defining which sub-goals may be pursued, acceptable side effects, and when to pause for clarification

seed_vocabulary.name: under_18_principles
seed_vocabulary.prose: the additional safety requirements that apply to users ages 13-17 in ChatGPT, prioritizing prevention, transparency, and early intervention

expected_cross_links.name: authority_level_ordering
expected_cross_links.evidence: child 2's chain-of-command rules and child 3's per-section authority tags rely on the ordering of authority levels established at L69-101 in child 1

expected_cross_links.name: candidate_instructions

expected_cross_links.name: applicable_instructions
expected_cross_links.evidence: child 3's no_other_objectives section relies on the applicable-instructions concept defined in child 2

expected_cross_links.name: stay_in_bounds_content_categories

expected_cross_links.name: transformation_exception

expected_cross_links.name: scope_of_autonomy

judgment_calls: Could have cut at L795 (end of chain of command) instead of L1120; chose L1120 because the stay-in-bounds section's content-category taxonomy (prohibited/restricted/sensitive) is established across L810-1116 and would have been split across children if cut at L795.

Could have cut child 3 at L2126 (start of seek the truth) or L3148 (start of best work); chose to keep it as one span because the sections are independent and the only cross-boundary dependencies are the seeded concepts, so a single large child is cleaner than multiple cuts that would each need their own seeds.

Seeded under_18_principles even though it is established entirely within child 3, because child 3's under-18 section references stay-in-bounds content categories from child 2 and the seed ensures the name is available for the cross-link.
